text:
Maya P: heads-up — EU2 has had 3 short tail-latency spikes in the last hour, all attributable to a single tenant id. KV cache churn + repeated preemptions. I'm thinking a quarantine flow (soft isolate) rather than a full preemptive drain.

Raj S: can you paste the query/metrics you used? want to replicate and check correlation with egress.

Maya P: https://dashboards.redwood/eu2/allocs -> filtered by tenant: T-8421. Top signals: gpu_wait_ms spike, kvcache_miss_rate up to 78%, and node_cpu_irq rising.

Maya P: quick log sample:
```
2026-03-19T18:02:12Z alloc=T-8421 host=eu2-rack12 node=gpu-09 gpu_wait_ms=412 kvcache_miss=0.78
2026-03-19T18:02:23Z alloc=T-8421 host=eu2-rack14 node=gpu-21 gpu_wait_ms=498 kvcache_miss=0.81
```

Sophia L: yikes. Is this noisy neighbor (IO/PCIe) or the tenant's batch job hammering memory?

Maya P: appears IO-side (DMA bursts) — NVLink counters show high pcie_tx during the spikes. Not typical model cache growth.

Liam G: quarantine flow = what exactly? spin up dedicated warm slice? restrict networking egress? or apply preemptible cap? cost implications matter.

Raj S: proposed quick heuristic for detection + auto action:
- detect when single tenant contributes >40% of 95p latency across the rack for 5m window
- confirm kvcache_miss_rate >60% and pcie_tx > baseline*3
- mark tenant as "noisy-suspect" and apply soft-quarantine: reduce concurrency to 1, pin to isolated pool, enable aggressive KV TTL
- if repeats 3 times in 1h, trigger canary migration to dedicated slice or manual review

Raj S: SQL-ish query we used in the probe (adapt for graphite/prom):
```
SELECT tenant, percentile(latency,95) as p95, avg(kvcache_miss_rate) as miss
FROM alloc_metrics
WHERE region='eu2' AND ts > now() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY tenant
ORDER BY p95 DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

Maya P: fleet-bot pulled the allocation timeline and created shortlink: https://fleet.redwood/alloc/T-8421/trace

fleet-bot: alert: tenant T-8421 matched noisy-suspect heuristic (p95=420ms, kvcache_miss=0.79) at 2026-03-19T18:03:30Z

Sophia L: If we pin them to a warm slice we pay ~0.6x extra for the period, but it removes collateral damage. Alternative: apply routing weight down to 0.3 and let clients retry -> increases latency but keeps cost low.

Liam G: need to flag customer-facing cost and SLA impact. If we move to dedicated slice for X hours, ops cost = estimated $1.2k for the slice in eu2. On the other hand, cascading retries cost us more at 95p across other tenants.

Maya P: short term plan I recommend:
1) apply soft-quarantine for 10m (reduce concurrency, aggressive KV TTL) now
2) if spike subsides -> auto-unquarantine + note in incident log
3) if spike returns within 30m -> schedule canary migration to a fractional dedicated slice and page oncall
4) post-mortem and contact tenant with suggested workload shaping

Raj S: +1. Add a metric annotation for cost delta for the canary (so PM/team can evaluate). Also add a temporary route fallback to a lower-cost quantized model variant if latency becomes catastrophic.

Sophia L: ops-bot, can you run the soft-quarantine step now and report back?

ops-bot: running action: apply_soft_quarantine tenant=T-8421 duration=600s modifiers=[concurrency=1, kv_ttl=30s, nic-police=rate:20mbps]

ops-bot: action result: success. quarantine started at 2026-03-19T18:04:12Z. Estimated immediate tail latency reduction ~45%.

Liam G: thanks. I'll open a cost estimate ticket for a 2h fractional-slice migration and ping sales for tenant communication.

Maya P: leaving this thread open for 1h. If p95 stays >300 after quarantine we escalate to migration. Current plan documented in runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/noise-quarantine

Raj S: followups:
- add a transient tag to the tenant allocation so billing can track slice-hours separately
- add probe to detect PCIe bursts (not just kvcache miss)

Sophia L: postmortem owner volunteer? I can take it if nobody else.

Liam G: Sophia can own. I will help with cost analysis.

Maya P: great — will update incident note and close if metrics normalize. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: metric update snapshot at 2026-03-19T18:09:00Z: p95=190ms (down from 420ms), kvcache_miss=0.42

Maya P: looks stable for now, marking as monitoring. Will reopen if we see recurrence.
